sources.title: January 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: BDUK publishes this release as monthly contract-level Project Gigabit management information.
The January table is a snapshot of data held on 20 January 2026.
Contracted figures cover initial scope and can exclude deferred-scope premises.
The figures are not directly comparable with official subsidy-attributable delivery statistics.
Values are rounded to the nearest 10 and ingestion lag prevents milestone assessment.

sources.title: February 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: The February release reports contract-level management information for Project Gigabit.
The table is a snapshot of data held on 16 February 2026.
Initial-scope contracted premises and built contracted premises are separate measures.
Variable delivery-to-ingestion lag means the data should not be used to judge contractual milestones.
Figures are rounded to the nearest 10 and may not sum exactly.

sources.title: March 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: The March publication is monthly contract-level management information.
The data snapshot date is 17 March 2026.
Deferred scope can be absent from the contracted-premises figures.
Management-information delivery counts differ conceptually from official subsidy-attributable statistics.
Rounded values and administrative ingestion lag require month-specific provenance.

sources.title: April 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: The April release reports Project Gigabit contracted and built premises by contract.
The table represents a snapshot held on 22 April 2026.
Only initial contract scope is represented in the contracted-premises field.
The release warns against direct comparison with official delivery statistics.
Figures are rounded to the nearest 10 and are unsuitable for contractual milestone assessment.

sources.title: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026
facts: The January 2026 NR OMR was published on 6 January 2026 and last updated on 10 June 2026.
It sought current and planned gigabit-capable infrastructure information over a three-year horizon.
The NR OMR runs in January, May and September.
The page links the Request for Information and the formal closure outcome.
The June update added links to regional outputs.

sources.title: National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026 Request For Information
facts: The RFI requests supplier information about existing and planned broadband infrastructure.
Supplier returns support premises-level assessment of commercial build over the next three years.
Responses require coverage data plus supporting evidence rather than unsupported assertions.
The process informs Project Gigabit subsidy eligibility and intervention-area design.
An RFI submission or eligibility classification is not evidence of an orderable service.

sources.title: Closure of the January 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
facts: The January NR OMR ran from 6 January to 6 February 2026 and supplier submissions were evaluated.
BDUK classified premises as White, Grey, Black or Under Review.
The England and Wales summary contained 31,054,557 premises across the four classifications.
Only White premises are subsidy targets; Under Review premises require further assessment.
Outputs are time-sensitive administrative classifications and include an explicit accuracy disclaimer.

sources.title: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026
facts: The May 2026 NR OMR ran from 1 May to 1 June 2026.
It requested premises-level information about existing and planned build over the next three years.
The consultation was open to suppliers across the UK.
The process is one of the January, May and September rolling reviews.
The index page links the RFI and closure notice as separate evidence objects.

sources.title: National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026 Request For Information
sources.lines: introduction, geographical scope, process and voucher-treatment sections
facts: The May RFI asks suppliers for premises-level current and planned build data.
BDUK uses supplier evidence with Ofcom Connected Nations information for assessment.
The assessed May outcome is limited to England and Wales despite wider data collection.
UPRN lists are sourced from AddressBase Premium Epoch 123 and divided into regional files.
Voucher-issued, voucher-claimed and pre-voucher premises receive different administrative treatment.

sources.title: Closure of the May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
facts: The May 2026 NR OMR closed at 5pm on 1 June 2026.
BDUK then began evaluating supplier coverage and evidence submissions.
The exercise informs intervention planning, GigaHubs and voucher eligibility.
Formal assessment for the May round covers England and Wales.
The closure notice says outputs will be published after evaluation and therefore is not a final coverage result.

sources.title: Key findings, Statistical Digest of Rural England
sources.lines: Connectivity and Accessibility key findings, July 2026
facts: The key-findings page was updated on 22 July 2026.
It states that the most rural areas lag the rest of England for decent, superfast and gigabit-capable availability.
Majority-rural constituencies have proportionally more voice, text, 4G and 5G not-spots.
The findings combine multiple thematic reports and are area-level summaries.
Rural classifications and denominators must be preserved before downstream comparison.
